create.name: Kwan Um Zen Belgium (Brussels Zen Center)
create.bio:
Kwan Um Zen Belgium is the Brussels centre of the Kwan Um School of Zen, the Korean Zen school founded by Zen Master Seung Sahn, which now has groups in around twenty countries. Its practice rooms are on Nestelingstraat in Sint-Jans-Molenbeek, and its retreats are led by Koen Vermeulen JDPSN. The centre describes its practice as returning, moment by moment, to the mind as it is before thinking arises, and acting from that clear mind with compassion for all beings. It is a member of the Buddhist Union of Belgium and names an integrity contact under the union's ethics charter.

Its main programme for newcomers and experienced students alike is Kompas voor het leven, a Wednesday evening course in Dutch that runs in parts: an introduction to Zen meditation through body, breath and sitting, an introduction to Buddhist teaching using mantra and self-enquiry, and practice in daily life. Each part can be joined on its own and is booked by email. Through the year the centre also holds one-day and weekend retreats in Brussels, including a day for beginners, and in 2026 it ran a week-long summer retreat at Mottereau in France. Supporting members pay a monthly fee that covers all activities except retreats.

courses.title: Kompas voor het leven: Introductie tot Zen meditatie
courses.description: The first part of the centre's Wednesday evening programme in Dutch: six sessions in Brussels on attention, breath, body awareness and sitting meditation, ending with a walk in silence nearby. Each part can be booked on its own by email.

courses.title: Retreat for beginners
courses.description: A one-day retreat at the Brussels centre for people new to Zen, led by Koen Vermeulen JDPSN.
